title: ConnPool backpressure, circuit breakers, and graceful degradation for downstream stores
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a targeted reliability initiative to harden runtime interactions with critical downstream stores (Redis, Kafka, Postgres). This ticket covers connection-pooling behavior under load, circuit-breaker policies, load-shedding rules, and graceful degradation patterns (cache-stale serving, reduced feature paths). The goal is to keep overall request-level SLOs stable during downstream degradation and to provide predictable fallbacks for caller services. Work spans runtime/client library changes, metrics/alerts, chaos tests, and a staged rollout behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: Connection pool implements dynamic backpressure and saturates gracefully without unbounded latency growth
Circuit breaker opens and isolates unhealthy downstream partitions within configured thresholds and auto-recovers after cooldown
Load-shedding policy exists to reject non-critical traffic with 503 and appropriate Retry-After headers when system is under sustained overload
Two graceful-degradation strategies implemented and selectable by route: stale-cache fallback and reduced-response-quality (token cap/shorter completion)
Automated canary validates behavior in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 with no SLO regressions for user-facing endpoints
Runbook updated with alert conditions and step-by-step mitigation instructions
decisions: Adopt a token-bucket based connection admission policy per downstream service rather than fixed max inflight to allow controlled bursts
Implement circuit breaker per-instance AND per-region to avoid cascading failures across regions
Use 95th/99th latency percentiles for dynamic pool resizing signals (EWMA-based) rather than instantaneous p95 spikes
Prioritize client-side defensive measures (local queue limits + early reject) before global routing changes
Expose feature-flag hooks to enable aggressive degradation per-customer for Dedicated/Private deployments
design_notes: Separate pools per downstream role (read-cache, kv-store, event-producer) to prevent cross-contamination
Pool sizing: base size = min(ceil(concurrency_per_cpu * cpus), 500); dynamic headroom = 20% of base resized by EWMA latency
Admission control: each request consumes a pool token; if none available, request waits up to 'max_wait_ms' then is rejected with a 503 and metrics emitted
Circuit-breaker thresholds: open when error rate > 15% for a 60s window AND p95 latency > 1.5x baseline; half-open test sends single-probe requests with conservative timeout
Backoff and retry: client retries only on idempotent ops with exponential backoff capped at 250ms and jitter; non-idempotent ops must not be auto-retried
Degradation modes: STALE_CACHE (serve cached response with 'X-Served-Stale' header) and REDUCED_QUALITY (limit generation length to configured token cap). Both must be opt-in per route
Multi-region failover: prefer local region pool; if region circuit is open, route to fallback region pool subject to cross-region cost thresholds and data residency tags
implementation_plan: runtime: add conn-pool middleware with token-bucket admission and per-pool EWMA telemetry (PR #5421)
client libraries: surface early-reject exceptions and Retry-After header handling (PR #5427)
circuit-breaker: implement per-instance state machine with metrics export and admin endpoints (PR #5433)
degradation: add STALE_CACHE and REDUCED_QUALITY handlers tied to route config (PR #5450)
infra: extend load-test rig to simulate Redis/Kafka partial outages and cross-region latency fuzzing (ENG-ops ticket ENG-20510)
docs: update runbooks and public behavior docs for API clients
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket admission logic and pool token accounting
Synthetic load tests: ramp to 2x peak QPS with induced Redis 500ms latency and 10% error injection; verify backpressure prevents tail latency blowup
Chaos tests: kill subset of Kafka brokers + simulating network partition between regions; assert circuit opens and fallbacks trigger
Canary: enable behind FF in eu-west-1 for 1% of traffic, monitor SLOs for 24h before scaling to 25%
Regression tests for client libraries handling Retry-After and early-reject exceptions
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge feature-flag guarded code to main and run full CI; deploy to canary fleet (eu-west-1) at 1%
Stage 2: If no SLO regressions, increase to 10% after 6h; validate internal dashboards and error budgets
Stage 3: Expand to 50% and then global with region-by-region enablement. If critical alerts fire, flip FF off and run postmortem
Stage 4: Promote to runtime-1.22 release and include configuration knobs in Console UI for Dedicated customers
monitoring_and_alerting: SLOs: user-request P99 latency < 350ms and error rate < 0.3% global; derive error budget burn from these metrics
New metrics: pool_tokens_total, pool_tokens_in_use, pool_wait_time_ms_p95, conn_admit_reject_rate, cb_open_count, degradation_rate_by_route
Alerts: SEV2 when pool_wait_time_ms_p95 > 200ms for 5m and conn_admit_reject_rate > 1% for 5m
SEV1: cb_open_count increases by > 50% in any region within 10 minutes or cross-region failover rate > 2%
Dashboards: per-region heatmap of pool saturation, CB state, dropped_request_count; add an SLO burn chart for affected routes
